profiles.label: General
profiles.summary: Use the ordinary Authorities workflow without court-specific restrictions.

profiles.label: Alberta Court of King’s Bench
profiles.summary: A complete, searchable book matching the authorities and pinpoint format used in the submissions.
requirements: Include the authorities cited in the submissions and match their paragraph or page numbering.
Avoid authorities already reproduced by another party; a joint book is recommended.
Include both official-language versions of relied-on federal enactments where applicable.

profiles.label: Alberta Court of Appeal
profiles.summary: Adds a hyperlinked Table of Authorities to the end of the Word filing; there is no separate book where a public link exists.
requirements: List each authority, its citation and a free publicly accessible hyperlink at the end of the filing.
Keep the authorities in first-reference order.
Do not reproduce a linked authority; if no public link exists, append and bookmark its copy.

profiles.label: Federal Court
profiles.summary: A searchable electronic book containing only relied-on authorities, with marked passages, bookmarks, tabs and an index.
requirements: Include only authorities referred to in the memorandum and clearly mark and bookmark the relied-on passages.
Use a numeric or alphabetical tab for every source and an index identifying each tab.
Avoid duplication after consulting other parties; a joint book is acceptable. Reproduce federal enactment extracts in both official languages.

profiles.label: Federal Court of Appeal
profiles.summary: A searchable appeal authorities book using the Federal Courts Rules order and electronic-document mechanics.
requirements: Include only authorities to be referred to at the hearing and mark the relied-on passages.
Use tabs and an index; avoid duplication and use a joint book where practical.
For paper filing, Rule 348 prescribes burgundy for a joint book and the memorandum colour for a separate book.
